title: Recipe 44 — Chain as typed-tool gateway (an ABI becomes tools at compile time)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “A contract ABI is already a typed interface. This recipe turns it into agent tools without you writing wrappers.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — nothing committed is touched by a take.

beats.label: Type the generator call
beats.cue: “generateContractTools — the recipe's TL;DR. It runs at compile time, so the tool list is fixed before the agent ever boots.”

beats.label: Prove it parses
beats.cue: “Real TypeScript, not pseudocode — the recipe's fence is a file you can keep.”
beats.command: bun -e 'const s = require("fs").readFileSync("live/generate.ts","utf8"); new Bun.Transpiler({ loader: "ts" }).transformSync(s); console.log("live/generate.ts: parses as TypeScript");'

verify.note: the recipe's generator fence is syntactically valid TS

beats.label: Open it
beats.cue: “One call per contract. The ABI is the schema — you don't write a JSON schema by hand.”

groups.title: Beat 2 · what a generated tool call looks like

beats.label: Type the call site
beats.cue: “usdc__balanceOf — contract, then double underscore, then the ABI method. The name is derived, so it can't drift.”

beats.label: Prove it parses
beats.cue: “Typed arguments, typed return. A misspelled field is a compile error, not a failed transaction.”
beats.command: bun -e 'const s = require("fs").readFileSync("live/call.ts","utf8"); new Bun.Transpiler({ loader: "ts" }).transformSync(s); console.log("live/call.ts: parses as TypeScript");'

verify.note: the recipe's call-site fence is syntactically valid TS

beats.label: Open it
beats.cue: “Read tools are free and idempotent. Write tools are the ones that need every gate recipe 43 puts up.”

groups.title: Beat 3 · a chain harness the gateway feeds

beats.label: Type recipe 47's treasury monitor
beats.cue: “Recipe 44 is a mechanism; this is a spec that uses it. Chain tools, declared in YAML.”

beats.label: Lint it
beats.cue: “Lint's §47 chain pass is what checks the ABI references resolve — this is the gate that catches a bad contract address.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “The chain tools are in the IR as ordinary typed tools. Nothing downstream knows they came from an ABI.”

beats.label: Open the IR
beats.cue: “That uniformity is the payoff: permissions, justification gates, and egress checks all apply to chain tools for free.”

beats.label: Check the bundle
beats.cue: “--check: GREEN, gated at the RPC credential. The generated tools survive a real install and boot.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the declared credentials gate

beats.label: Read shapes 5 and 7
beats.cue: “Multi-chain and proof-carrying — the two extensions that fall out once tools are typed rather than hand-written.”
